title: BNM establishes regulatory framework for open finance
text:
BNM establishes regulatory framework for open finance Tuesday 17 Nov 2026 BURSA SGX Home

 KUALA LUMPUR (Nov 17): Bank Negara Malaysia's rules on inter-bank sharing of customer data under the open finance framework will take effect on Jan 1, 2028, a year later than initially proposed.   
 Under the open finance framework proposed last year, people and businesses can consent to their information being shared across multiple financial service providers (FSP) so that they get access to more personalised financial services, manage accounts in multiple institutions through a single platform and simplify applications for financial products.
Certain financial institutions must be part of the open finance framework, but it is up to customers to allow the sharing of their financial information.
 The framework was initially slated for roll-out on Jan 1, 2027.  
 Under a policy document issued on Tuesday, financial institutions will be required to provide customers’ transaction history for the most recent 12 months, including the date, time, amount and description of transactions, as well as outstanding account balances, upon obtaining customers’ consent.
 This will cover savings accounts, current accounts, fixed deposits, Islamic deposit products, e-money accounts, charge cards and credit cards, where applicable.
 BNM requires customer consent to be specific, voluntary, explicit and revocable, prohibiting financial institutions from obtaining consent through pre-ticked boxes or blanket consent agreements.
 “A customer must explicitly opt in or deliberately agree to the disclosure of their information to a data consumer by taking an active step to indicate consent,” the policy document read.
 The framework also sets out requirements for data protection, cybersecurity, fraud risk management and complaint handling.
 “By enabling consent-driven information sharing, open finance is intended to provide customers with greater control over their personal financial information, allowing them to actively determine and manage how their information is shared, accessed and used,” BNM said.
 Beyond facilitating data sharing, the central bank will also require mandated financial institutions to develop digital interfaces allowing customers to view information from accounts held with other financial service providers.
 Financial institutions will also be required to facilitate the digital retrieval of customer information from other institutions, replacing conventional methods of document submission such as manually uploading or emailing bank statements.
 Other potential applications identified by BNM include improving credit underwriting through access to real-time financial information, enhancing fraud detection and expanding access to financial services.
 The sharing of financial information under the framework will be facilitated through Open Finance Malaysia (OFM), a platform operated by Payments Network Malaysia Sdn Bhd (PayNet).
 Phased roll-out according to FSP size 
 Conventional and Islamic banks with more than one million active individual and small and medium enterprise (SME) customers combined, either at the entity or banking group level, will be required to share customers’ financial information from Jan 1, 2028.
 The deadline will be extended to Jan 1, 2029, for banks with more than 250,000 customers and for e-money issuers with more than five million users.
 By then, these institutions must also have the digital interfaces for customers to access their information in other financial service providers.
 Development financial institutions with more than 250,000 active customers will be required to participate as both providers and recipients of financial data from Jan 1, 2030.
 Sharing of SMEs' financial information will also commence on the same date for mandated institutions with more than 30,000 active SME customers.
 Participation by investment banks, insurers and takaful operators will remain voluntary.
 Open finance is part of BNM’s digitalisation agenda under its Financial Sector Blueprint 2022-2026, which envisages greater accessibility and sharing of data within and beyond the financial sector.
 In November last year, the central bank issued an exposure draft on open finance.
 “BNM also envisions that the principles underpinning open finance can support broader arrangements for more open and secure data sharing beyond the financial industry,” the central bank said.
